content: Pregnant women who have a history of venous thromboembolism (VTE), antithrombin deficiency, or other risk factors for VTE require prophylactic treatment with heparin. This is typically administered subcutaneously, using either unfractionated heparin (UFH) or low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH). Various methods for subcutaneous administration of heparin have been developed to prevent adverse pregnancy outcomes. However, the effectiveness and safety of these different methods have not been systematically evaluated. The objective of this review was to compare the effectiveness and safety of different methods of administering subcutaneous heparin (UFH or LMWH) to pregnant women. To achieve this, a search was conducted in the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register up to January 31, 2013, as well as in the reference lists of relevant studies. The inclusion criteria for this review were all randomized controlled trials (both individual and cluster trials) that compared the effectiveness and safety of different methods of administering subcutaneous heparin during pregnancy. Studies that were only available as abstracts were eligible for inclusion and would have been placed in a category awaiting further assessment until full publication of their results. However, quasi-randomized studies and cross-over trials were excluded from consideration. The methods of administration under evaluation included intermittent injections, indwelling catheters, programmable (automatic) external infusion pumps, or any other devices designed to facilitate subcutaneous administration of heparin during pregnancy. If eligible trials had been identified, the quality of the trials would have been assessed, and data would have been extracted independently by the review authors without blinding. However, no trials met the inclusion criteria for this review. As a result, there is currently no evidence from randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of different methods of administering subcutaneous heparin (UFH or LMWH) to pregnant women.
